To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we developed a testing infrastructure to experimentally characterize the threshold voltage distribution in modern NAND flash memory, (ii) we devised a model of the distributions that takes into account the effects of P/E cycles, and (iii) we showed that the distributions can be modeled as a Gaussian distribution plus white noise, which widens as the P/E cycles increase.

we present the first published experimental characterization of the threshold distribution in MLC flash memory, and we develop a model that captures the evolution of the threshold distribution over P/E cycles.
the threshold voltage distributions of modern MLC NAND flash memories can be modeled as Gaussian distributions with additive white noise.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of P/E cycle-induced degradation, the threshold voltage distribution is best modeled as a Gaussian distribution.

threshold voltage distributions can be accurately modeled as a combination of a Gaussian distribution and white noise, which can be used to predict the distribution at a given number of program/erase cycles, and that this model is more accurate than a simple Gaussian model, which does not account for the noise.
